keyFindings.text: **006 — a flow grant is weaker than a tool grant for an effect the module cannot label.** For the `Unlabelled` row, a whole-tool grant approves it as an audited `auto:tool-grant`, but "neither `auto_approve_all` nor a flow grant approves it". [SOURCE: specs/system-skilled-bots/context/openhuman-full/vendor/tinysecurity/docs/module-approval-contracts.md:91] *(observed)* The plan's ladder is a single ordered list, so it cannot express a grant whose strength depends on the effect class. If 006 keeps one ladder, it must at least record that a flow-scoped grant does not cover an unclassified action.

**006 — a grant may convert a required approval into an automatic one and may override nothing else.** `ApprovalGrants2` carries "exact tool names, and exact tool names inside one named flow"; a grant "only converts a required approval into an automatic one (`auto:tool-grant`, `auto:flow-grant`)" and "never overrides a denial, a Cron external effect, reviewed reuse or a human-only tool (`HUMAN_ONLY_TOOLS2`, `native_*`)". "Names are never wildcards." [SOURCE: specs/system-skilled-bots/context/openhuman-full/vendor/tinysecurity/docs/module-approval-contracts.md:35-41] *(observed)* This is the missing half of the plan's ladder: the plan records the order in which a decision is reached but not the four things a grant may not reach past. A builder writing `grants` on a needs-you item needs the non-override list as a field-level rule, not as prose.

**006 — OpenBot classifies a decision by the tool left waiting, not by the action's verb.** `DECISION_TOOLS` maps `askApproval` to `approval` and `askChoice` and `askForm` to `question`, and the server "watches runs for a call to one that is left waiting, which is what puts the Bot under Needs you". [SOURCE: specs/system-skilled-bots/context/OpenBot-main/shared/decision-tools.ts:13-17] *(observed)* The plan's 006 adds an `action-kind.ts` that classifies the action. The two disagree on what makes an item a needs-you item: OpenBot counts a waiting decision tool, the plan counts an action kind. The evidence supports keeping both — the action kind for the grant, the waiting tool for the count — and the plan should say so, because a run that asks with a plain question would otherwise not appear under needs-you.

**006 — OpenBot's standing answer is three exclusions, not a rung.** `offersStandingRule` returns false when `policy.source === "task"`, when `policy.closed === true`, or when `policy.behaviour === "hand_off"`; only then does the card offer "Always allow here" or "Allow for this conversation". A task started from a check-in "asks before every change whatever the person's rules say", so a standing answer saved from one "would be ignored the next time and only mislead". [SOURCE: specs/system-skilled-bots/context/OpenBot-main/shared/standing-rule.ts:21-29] *(observed)* The plan's ladder is four rungs in order — kinds of action, rules, auto-review, extra vigilant — and says nothing about which approvals may take a standing answer. Phase 002's routines raise exactly the check-in-origin case this predicate excludes, so 006 needs the exclusion or a routine's first approval silently becomes permanent. The earlier synthesis carries the rung order only. [SOURCE: specs/system-skilled-bots/002-openbot-parity-research/001-openbot-parity-research/research/research.md:89]

**006 — the bot-voice leak has a test shape the plan lacks.** Every sentence the server answers a step with is exported from one file, and "`server/tests/approval-outcomes-for-person.test.ts` walks these exports and the approval service's, and fails on any that a person would still read in the words written for the Bot, so a sentence added later cannot leak by being forgotten here". [SOURCE: specs/system-skilled-bots/context/OpenBot-main/shared/approval-outcomes.ts:12-16] *(observed)* The plan's 006 adds a grant and a ladder and no test that a person-facing string is not written in the bot's voice. Phase 012 owns the scenario; the export-and-walk test belongs to 006.

**006 and 007 — a widening change must re-ask a human, and only a human answer counts.** `SupersedePolicy` returns `ReviewRequired` when the replacement "widens authority (new or broader roots, removed restrictions, new hosts or tools, higher command autonomy, classes, allowlist entries or budget ... new auto origins, judge enabled, enforcement or the registered path scope disabled, or privacy loosened)", and "Only a row decided by an authenticated human qualifies; automatic, judge and reused approvals are refused. A narrowing change activates without review." [SOURCE: specs/system-skilled-bots/context/openhuman-full/vendor/tinysecurity/docs/module-subject-policies.md:34-44] *(observed)* Phase 007's `apps:` key is a widening surface: adding a server to `apps:` grants a bot a capability it did not have. The plan's 007 has `apps-unknown-server` for a name that is not a known server, and no rule that a widened `apps:` list re-asks. The evidence supports adding one.

**007 — a per-run tool filter must not remove a tool the harness runs itself.** `HARNESS_OWN_TOOLS` is `ToolSearch` and `Read`: tools "a harness runs itself, inside its own run, and never hands to OpenBot or the browser", and "Nobody outside the harness answers it, so it never makes the caller the one to answer". [SOURCE: specs/system-skilled-bots/context/OpenBot-main/shared/harness-own-tools.ts:1-14] *(observed)* Phase 007 writes a filtered UTCP config per run. A filter that drops a tool the harness owns leaves the run waiting for an answer no one will give, which is a hang rather than a refusal. The plan's 007 has no harness-owned exclusion list.

**007 and 008 — the token compare to mirror is length-first and branch-free.** `matchesToken` returns false on an empty expected value or a length mismatch, then XOR-accumulates every code unit and compares the accumulator to zero. [SOURCE: specs/system-skilled-bots/context/OpenBot-main/shared/agent-authorisation.ts:2-9] *(observed)* The plan's REQ-011 already requires a constant-time read-back compare [SOURCE: specs/system-skilled-bots/003-openbot-parity-build/008-vault/spec.md:165], so this adds the shape rather than the requirement.

**008 — a backend error must be mapped to a fixed refusal, because the raw error can echo the value.** rakazo's `secretAnswerRefusal` maps a server error onto one of three fixed answers precisely because "Its other errors could echo the value, so they are never shown". [SOURCE: specs/system-skilled-bots/context/rakazo-main/packages/core/src/integrations/vault.ts:26-38] *(observed)* The plan's `secret-store-unreadable` prints `bots: secret-store-unreadable: <detail>`. [SOURCE: specs/system-skilled-bots/003-openbot-parity-build/contracts/refusals.md:160] *(observed)* If `<detail>` is the keychain program's own stderr, a failing write can print the value it failed to store. The plan needs a rule that `<detail>` is a fixed phrase per cause, never a captured backend message. This is the leak the plan's own threat model does not list.

**008 — rakazo's placeholder guard is environment-gated, and the gate is the bug to leave behind.** `isDevSecretAllowed` returns true for `RAKAZO_ALLOW_DEV_SECRETS=1`, for `VITEST` set to `true` or `1`, and for `NODE_ENV` of `development` or `test`; the placeholder is then accepted instead of refused. [SOURCE: specs/system-skilled-bots/context/rakazo-main/packages/core/src/node/secrets-guard.ts:25-30] *(observed)* The plan's `secret-placeholder` refusal is a fixed list with no environment gate. [SOURCE: specs/system-skilled-bots/003-openbot-parity-build/008-vault/design/leak-checks.md:30] *(observed)* Lift the placeholder list; do not lift `isDevSecretAllowed`, or a `NODE_ENV=development` shell turns the refusal off.

**008 — the lifted matcher carries two bounds the plan does not name.** `createSecretMatcher` builds an Aho–Corasick automaton over UTF-16 code units, caps it at `MAX_SECRET_MATCHER_STATES = 1_000_000` states, and past that falls back to scanning each value in turn; it also decides between the two by a `BUILD_COST = 8` work model. [SOURCE: specs/system-skilled-bots/context/rakazo-main/packages/core/src/messages/secret-matcher.ts:2,21,27,58] *(observed)* The plan's REQ-013 requires the one-pass matcher so "many stored values cost one pass over the text rather than one scan per value". [SOURCE: specs/system-skilled-bots/003-openbot-parity-build/008-vault/spec.md:167] *(observed)* It carries neither the state cap nor the fallback, so a builder who lifts the automaton without them gets unbounded memory on a long value. Lift the cap and the fallback with the matcher.

**008 — tinysecurity is GPL-3.0, so its contract text may be read and never copied.** The vendored crate's licence is "GNU GENERAL PUBLIC LICENSE Version 3". [SOURCE: specs/system-skilled-bots/context/openhuman-full/vendor/tinysecurity/LICENSE:1-2] *(observed)* The plan lifts only rakazo, which is Apache-2.0. [SOURCE: specs/system-skilled-bots/context/rakazo-main/LICENSE:1-2] *(observed)* The plan is therefore right to leave tinysecurity out of `THIRD_PARTY_NOTICES.md`, but a builder who reads findings 2 to 4 above must restate the rules in the plan's own words. This is the one licence hazard in the trust slice and no earlier synthesis names it.

**Evidence limit — the OpenBot snapshot has no `server/`, so the ladder's lower rungs are readable only as prose.** `shared/standing-rule.ts` cites `server/src/approvals/policy.ts`, `service.ts` and `store.ts`, and `shared/decision-tools.ts` cites `server/src/approvals/decision-waits.ts`; none of those paths exists in the vendored tree. `shared/sensitive-rule.test.ts` is present with no `shared/sensitive-rule.ts` beside it. [SOURCE: specs/system-skilled-bots/context/OpenBot-main/shared/standing-rule.ts:6-8] *(observed)* Rungs 2 to 4 of the plan's ladder therefore rest on `docs/approvals.md` alone, and the plan's own handoff criterion already marks them not implemented in this phase. Any later phase that implements rung 2 needs a different reference than this snapshot.

**003 — the sanitizer the plan specifies differs from the reference in one decision worth recording.** `safe_text` keeps every character except a control character, and keeps `\n`. [SOURCE: specs/system-skilled-bots/context/openhuman-full/crates/openhuman-tui/src/theme.rs:88-93] *(observed)* The plan's `theme::printable` *replaces* control characters rather than dropping them [SOURCE: specs/system-skilled-bots/003-openbot-parity-build/003-terminal-screen/spec.md:247] *(observed)*. Replacing is the better choice for a snapshot test, because a dropped character changes the display width silently while a replacement keeps the cell count stable. The plan is right and does not say why; 014 should record the reason so a later reviewer does not "simplify" it back to a drop.

**003 — the TUI's activity model is six states, and the plan's seven groups are the better fit.** `Status` is `Running`, `Success`, `Error`, `Waiting`, `Cancelled`, `Unknown`, with labels `running`, `done`, `failed`, `needs input`, `cancelled`, `stale` and one marker glyph each. [SOURCE: specs/system-skilled-bots/context/openhuman-full/crates/openhuman-tui/src/activity.rs:7-36] *(observed)* The plan's 001 groups rows under OpenBot's seven ids. The two disagree on `stale`: openhuman makes it a run state, the plan makes it a property of the index, and the plan's 003 header already reads a staleness flag separately. The evidence supports the plan. What is worth mirroring is the marker table, because a six-glyph table with a distinct marker per state is what makes a snapshot test assert a state rather than a sentence.

**009 — `tinyskills` is the one vendor crate whose subject the plan has and whose implementation it lacks.** It is "a host-independent Rust library for agentskills.io-style skill bundles" that parses them. [SOURCE: specs/system-skilled-bots/context/openhuman-full/vendor/tinyskills/README.md:1] *(observed)* 237 Rust files, 78,138 lines. The plan's 009 injects a `skills:` list body at a position and refuses `skills-over-budget`; it has no bundle parser and no name grammar. Value to a small team: **high**, size **M** — the parse rules are the part 009 needs and the injection is the part it already has. Read for the grammar, lift nothing.

**011 — `tinychannels` is a full multi-channel runtime, far past what 011 needs.** 731 Rust files, 273,669 lines. [SOURCE: specs/system-skilled-bots/context/openhuman-full/vendor/tinychannels/README.md:1] *(observed)* The plan's 011 is a link roster, an answer gate and a send queue over a fake transport. Value: **low**, size **XL**. The one idea worth taking is that the channel layer is a module behind a bus rather than a branch in the runner.

**012 — the test corpus to mirror is one `*_tests.rs` beside every module, not a scenario file per behaviour.** `openhuman-tui/src/` holds `account_tests.rs`, `actions_tests.rs`, `app_tests.rs`, `browser_login_tests.rs`, `cockpit_tests.rs`, `composer_tests.rs`, `controls_tests.rs`, `crash_reporting_tests.rs`, `demo_tests.rs`, `effects_tests.rs`, `event_view_tests.rs` and `input_tests.rs`, each beside the module it tests. [SOURCE: specs/system-skilled-bots/context/openhuman-full/crates/openhuman-tui/src/activity_tests.rs:1] *(observed)* The plan's 012 is 33 scenario files keyed by behaviour id. The two are complementary: the plan's scenarios prove a verb end to end, and a per-module test file is what keeps a module's own edge cases from being reachable only through the CLI. 012 should add the second shape for the 003 crate, which is the one place the plan builds a module with internal state.

**013 and 014 — the upgrade path the plan lacks is a feature-forwarding check.** `openhuman-tui/Cargo.toml` states that "every gate forwards to `openhuman-rpc` alone (chain: core -> embed -> tinyhumans -> rpc -> app/cli/tui); `scripts/ci/check-feature-forwarding.mjs` checks the link", and that the default set "used to arrive implicitly through a bare workspace `openhuman-core` dependency, which turned on the core's whole `default`". [SOURCE: specs/system-skilled-bots/context/openhuman-full/crates/openhuman-tui/Cargo.toml:9-18] *(observed)* That is a real upgrade failure — a feature set that silently widened because a dependency was declared bare — with a script that catches it. The plan's 003 pins a toolchain and runs `cargo clippy` and `cargo test` and has no equivalent check. 013 should own the doc line and 014 the check.

**Net-new — `openhuman-full` differs from `openhuman-main` by the vendor tree and nothing else.** `openhuman-full` holds 29,050 files against `openhuman-main`'s 7,718, and the whole difference is `vendor/`: 21,332 files in `openhuman-full`, zero in `openhuman-main`. Every other top-level directory carries the identical count in both trees — `crates/` 4,497, `app/` 2,197, `scripts/` 432, `tests/` 217, `docs/` 209, `packages/` 42, `fastlane/` 16. [SOURCE: specs/system-skilled-bots/context/openhuman-full/vendor/tinysecurity/Cargo.toml:1] *(observed)* So the only thing a run gains by reading `openhuman-full` is the vendor tree. Reading it for anything else is reading `openhuman-main` twice.

**Net-new — `openhuman-tui` is in both trees, so the topic's second premise is also wrong.** `openhuman-main/crates/openhuman-tui/src/theme.rs` exists, and the plan's own 003 already cites it. [SOURCE: specs/system-skilled-bots/context/openhuman-main/crates/openhuman-tui/src/theme.rs:88] *(observed)* What `openhuman-full` adds is a *built* artifact, not a crate: `openhuman-full.build.log` ends `Finished dev profile [unoptimized + debuginfo] target(s) in 4m 33s` after `openhuman-tui (bin "openhuman-tui") generated 1 warning`. [SOURCE: specs/system-skilled-bots/context/openhuman-full.build.log:1] *(observed)* The build log is the only evidence in either tree that the TUI compiles, and it is worth one line in 014's review checklist rather than a phase of its own.

**Net-new — `tinybus` is the architectural idea behind the whole vendor tree and the plan has no bus.** It is "a zbus-style message bus that keeps external integrations out of the OpenHuman kernel's dependency". [SOURCE: specs/system-skilled-bots/context/openhuman-full/vendor/tinybus/README.md:1] *(observed)* 172 Rust files, 79,755 lines. The plan's runtime calls its integrations directly. Value: **medium**, size **L** — worth recording as the reason the twenty-one crates exist, not worth building.

**Net-new — `tinydocs` is the only document-output path in any of the ten repos.** It writes `.docx` and `.pptx` and reads them back. [SOURCE: specs/system-skilled-bots/context/openhuman-full/vendor/tinydocs/README.md:1] *(observed)* 226 Rust files, 83,976 lines. No 003 phase produces a document; a bot that must hand a person a file has no verb for it. Value: **medium**, size **M**.

**Net-new — `tinyeventqueues` is the highest-value crate the plan has no counterpart for.** It is "external event management and queuing ... a TinyBus module that receives noisy inbound events". [SOURCE: specs/system-skilled-bots/context/openhuman-full/vendor/tinyeventqueues/README.md:1] *(observed)* 262 Rust files, 89,431 lines. The plan's only queue is 011's *outbound* send queue; nothing dedupes or orders an *inbound* event, and 002's cron and 011's channel both produce inbound events. Value to a small team: **high**, size **M**. This is the one net-new item worth a phase.

**Net-new — `tinywallet` is the one crate that is a liability rather than a candidate.** It is "agent-friendly multi-chain wallet primitives". [SOURCE: specs/system-skilled-bots/context/openhuman-full/vendor/tinywallet/README.md:1] *(observed)* 420 Rust files, 129,856 lines. The plan's 006 defers "pay" to a later packet, so a wallet is a payment surface with no approval rung above it. Value: **negative**, and 014 should name it as a thing the plan is right to omit.

**Net-new — every one of the twenty-one vendor crates is GPL-3.0, so the whole tree is read-only design evidence.** The workspace manifest fixes `license = "GPL-3.0-only"` [SOURCE: specs/system-skilled-bots/context/openhuman-full/Cargo.toml:35] and each crate carries the GPL-3.0 text [SOURCE: specs/system-skilled-bots/context/openhuman-full/vendor/tiny-artifacts/LICENSE:1] *(observed)*. The plan's 003 already reaches the right conclusion for the wrong reason — it says "no third-party code is copied, so there is nothing to notice" [SOURCE: specs/system-skilled-bots/003-openbot-parity-build/003-terminal-screen/spec.md:118] *(observed)*, when the reason is that the reference is GPL-3.0 and copying it would relicense the crate. This is the single most important net-new finding: the answer to "what do the ten repos have that the plan misses" is twenty-one crates that may be read and never lifted.

**Net-new — six crates are out of scope by the skip list or by the plan's own deferral, and should be recorded as such rather than re-examined.** `tinyconnectors` is "OAuth connector integrations" [SOURCE: specs/system-skilled-bots/context/openhuman-full/vendor/tinyconnectors/README.md:1], which the skip list already rules out; `tinybox` is "a workspace containerization runtime" [SOURCE: specs/system-skilled-bots/context/openhuman-full/vendor/tinybox/README.md:1], also skipped; `tinycomputer` is "a decision model (Jev) based harness for desktop and browser automation" [SOURCE: specs/system-skilled-bots/context/openhuman-full/vendor/tinycomputer/README.md:1], which 004 does not do; `tinyhosts` puts "a Next.js application ... on a real hosting provider" [SOURCE: specs/system-skilled-bots/context/openhuman-full/vendor/tinyhosts/README.md:1]; `tinyhumans-sdk` is "a Rust client for the public TinyHumans backend API" [SOURCE: specs/system-skilled-bots/context/openhuman-full/vendor/tinyhumans-sdk/README.md:1]; and `tinymcp` is "a production-ready Rust 2024 TinyBus module template" [SOURCE: specs/system-skilled-bots/context/openhuman-full/vendor/tinymcp/README.md:1] *(all observed)*. Value: **none** for each, size **S** to record and **XL** to build.

**Net-new — the premise is wrong on the count: `openhuman-full` vendors twenty-one crates, not five.** The vendor tree holds `tiny-artifacts`, `tinyagents`, `tinybox`, `tinybus`, `tinychannels`, `tinycomputer`, `tinyconnectors`, `tinydocs`, `tinyeventqueues`, `tinyflows`, `tinyhosts`, `tinyhumans-sdk`, `tinyjuice`, `tinymcp`, `tinymemory`, `tinysearch`, `tinysecurity`, `tinyskills`, `tinystoragedrivers`, `tinyvoice` and `tinywallet`. [SOURCE: specs/system-skilled-bots/context/openhuman-full/vendor/tinybus/README.md:1] *(observed, by directory listing)* The five the topic names are a subset. This matters because the net-new answer is not five crates to weigh but twenty-one, and the ranking below is what makes that tractable.

**006 — the plan's `grants` field has no place for the effect class, so iteration 1's finding 3 lands as a field gap.** The plan's grant holds "the action kind, the action in the bot's words, the rung that made it ask and the scope the answer granted". [SOURCE: specs/system-skilled-bots/003-openbot-parity-build/006-approval-grants/spec.md:50] *(observed)* tinysecurity's grant strength depends on the effect class: a whole-tool grant approves an `Unlabelled` effect while a flow grant does not. [SOURCE: specs/system-skilled-bots/context/openhuman-full/vendor/tinysecurity/docs/module-approval-contracts.md:91] *(observed)* Four fields cannot express that. Either the grant gains an effect-class field or 006 records that a flow-scoped grant is out of scope, which is the cheaper answer for a phase that implements rung 1 only.

**006 — the reference composes checks, and the plan's ladder does not.** `Check::HostTool` "lets the host request approval for a tool whose effect the module cannot inspect", "alone it is `approval_unavailable`, which the approval path treats as \"needs a human\"", and "it never relaxes a `Path` or `Command` check carried beside it". [SOURCE: specs/system-skilled-bots/context/openhuman-full/vendor/tinysecurity/docs/module-approval-contracts.md:45-48] *(observed)* The plan's 006 applies rung 1 at the needs-you gate only, so two checks on one call cannot compose. The evidence supports the plan for a phase that implements rung 1, and the composition rule is what a later phase needs; 006 should record it as the shape rung 2 inherits.

**007 — the checker and the runner share one predicate, which is the pattern the rest of the packet should copy.** "The checker imports the same predicate the runner calls, so a name the runner would refuse fails the check first." [SOURCE: specs/system-skilled-bots/003-openbot-parity-build/007-per-bot-apps/design/state-machines.md:221] *(observed)* That is the same one-declaration-read-from-both-sides pattern as OpenBot's `DECISION_TOOLS` and `offersStandingRule`. [SOURCE: specs/system-skilled-bots/context/OpenBot-main/shared/decision-tools.ts:13-17] *(observed)* The plan has the pattern in 007 and not in 006 or 008, where the checker and the runner each carry their own copy of the rule. 014 should name the three places and ask for one.

**008 — the plan's `secret-store-unreadable` fails closed on every surface, which is stronger than the reference.** "The runner refuses `secret-store-unreadable` before the loop. `answerItem` refuses `secret-store-unreadable` with exit 4. `deliverRecord` sets each queued entry `not-attempted` with the evidence `withheld: secret-store-unreadable`. None of them falls back to the environment-only map, because a check that silently drops the vault would pass the very value it exists to stop." [SOURCE: specs/system-skilled-bots/003-openbot-parity-build/008-vault/design/leak-checks.md:61] *(observed)* rakazo's `isDevSecretAllowed` is exactly the silent fallback this rules out. [SOURCE: specs/system-skilled-bots/context/rakazo-main/packages/core/src/node/secrets-guard.ts:25-30] *(observed)* The plan is right and the reference is the counter-example; 008 should cite it as such so a builder does not "simplify" the fail-closed path into a fallback.

**F-2-007 — but the plan has no rule for a *displayed* tool name, and OpenBot found that failure live.** OpenBot puts any tool name in words, "never drawn as it came", because "FOUND LIVE: a Bot first called `web_search`, a name it was never offered, and its line read \"web_search\" until the real search joined it". [SOURCE: specs/system-skilled-bots/context/OpenBot-main/shared/tool-name.ts:20-27] *(observed)* The plan's 001 activity rows carry seven row keys and a text form fixed in `design/data-model.md` section 7, with no name-in-words rule. [SOURCE: specs/system-skilled-bots/003-openbot-parity-build/001-activity-and-actor/spec.md:166] *(observed)* A tool name drawn raw is the exact failure OpenBot already hit, and the plan's 003 sanitizer does not cover it because a raw name is printable text, not a control character.

**F-2-007 — the 64-character provider cap forces a shortened name with a hash, and the plan has no mapping back.** "A provider takes a tool name of at most 64 characters, so a long app action travels cut and ended with a hash: `mcp__composio-googlesheets__GOOGLESHEETS_UPDATE_DIMENSI_82883606`. Read as it stands, its step said \"Update dimensi 82883606\". A hash does not read backwards, so whoever shortened the names says what they stand for."
